transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-19
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samir Rao (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM); Elena Vazquez (ArgentCloud Principal Architect), Marc Huang (ArgentCloud ML Eng), Sofia Ruiz (ArgentCloud Security), Tom Keller (ArgentCloud PM)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect):
ArgentCloud is evaluating replacing their current managed LLM layer with Redwood for lower tail latency and better cost controls. Primary use is a function-calling workflow that routes to internal tools and an internal knowledge base. They need OpenAI-compat SDK calls, structured JSON output, and deterministic function outputs for compliance. Want a POC that proves parity on accuracy and improves 95th/99th latency under load.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Okay hi everyone, thanks for joining, real quick intros — I think we all have the roster, I'll let Samir lead on the technical scoping portion and I'll cover commercial/next steps at the end.
[00:22] Elena V.: Thanks Jordan, yeah we have a tight timeline — legal wants a recommended vendor by mid June. I'll be taking notes on success criteria and timings.
[00:35] Samir Rao: Cool, so high level — ArgentCloud, you mentioned earlier in the form you run two main workflows: chat-like assistant that triggers tools and a batch rerank job, is that still accurate?
[00:50] Marc Huang: Yeah that's right. The conversational assistant handles user queries and then sometimes invokes our internal inventory service, order service, or a custom document fetcher. Rerank runs nightly to surface top customer tickets.
[01:05] Tom K.: We're most concerned about the assistant flow — function-calling determinism, strict JSON schemas for downstream services, and latency spikes when traffic bursts.
[01:17] Samir: Got it. A couple questions to size things — what's your steady QPS and peak QPS, and average prompt/token lengths?
[01:28] Marc: Steady is around 8 qps across the fleet, peaks up to 65 qps during promos. Average prompt size is 500 tokens including system + user context, but we have long-context cases up to 4k tokens for full conversation history.
[01:45] Jordan: When you say 65 qps is that concurrent requests or calls including rerank?
[01:50] Marc: That's total calls; rerank is more batch and we can schedule it off-peak. The assistant is the bursty real-time traffic.
[02:02] Samir: Great. For the POC we typically recommend replicating the assistant traffic (latency-sensitive) at 20-30 qps and running a separate batch benchmark for rerank at throughput. That gives a realistic picture. Does that map to what you want?
[02:16] Elena: Yes, if you can show 95th under 250ms for typical 500-token prompts that's huge for us. Our current provider averages 95th around 420ms during bursts.
[02:29] Sofia R.: Also we need evidence of data segregation and KMS integration — we can't send customer PII blind; any sample payloads must be anonymized.
[02:40] Samir: Understood, we'll run on synthetic/anonymized payloads, and we can also run a VPC test if you prefer Redwood Private — that'll be later in the pilot if needed. For the benchmark we offer two modes: Redwood-hosted or Private VPC bench. Hosted is faster to run.
[02:56] Marc: Hosted is fine for initial run, but security wants to see the VPC option documented.
[03:05] Jordan: We'll include a short doc comparing Hosted vs Private bench process and the steps to onboard to Private.

[03:12] Elena: Let's talk about function calling. Right now we use OpenAI-style function calls where model returns a JSON with name and args. Can Redwood's OpenAI-compatible endpoints map 1:1 to our current client code?
[03:27] Samir: Yes — Redwood supports OpenAI-consistent endpoints and SDK wrappers. For functions we support the same name/args pattern and also Redwood's structured-output enforcement which can validate and schema-check before returning. Small caveat: some of our internal optimizations like prefix caching and KV cache can change tokenization behavior slightly but not the function payload semantics.
[03:51] Marc: Are there any differences in the schema enforcement? We need strict validation because downstream systems fail if fields missing.
[03:58] Samir: We can configure strict schema validation and we also offer automatic retries with a structured-output fallback. If validation fails we can optionally route to a lightweight rule-based filler to avoid downstream exceptions.
[04:14] Sofia: That retry behavior — is the retry logged/auditable? We need full tracing for SOC2.
[04:21] Priya Nair: Yes, audit logs include request/response and retry events, and we keep them in the tenant's audit log with S3 retention you can configure. We'll share the exact retention options in the security package.
[04:34] Tom: On SDKs — we use the OpenAI SDK across backend services in Node and Python. Is Redwood's SDK a drop-in?
[04:44] Samir: We aim for drop-in compatibility for the major call types. There are tiny naming differences around streaming hooks but we have migration notes. We can run a short migration test: point one service at Redwood-hosted OpenAI-compat endpoint and run smoke tests.

[05:00] Elena: Benchmarks — what's your recommended harness? We need reproducible scripts and a clear measurement spec.
[05:08] Samir: We'll provide a benchmark harness repo that uses your anonymized payloads, supports steady-state QPS and spike tests, and measures p50/p95/p99, cold-start tail, and per-token cost. It will also validate structured output correctness against your schemas.
[05:26] Marc: Do you support instrumenting our tracing (e.g., OTEL) so we can combine Redwood traces with our app traces?
[05:33] Samir: Yes we support OpenTelemetry hooks and you can add trace ids in request metadata. We'll include a trace-merge guide.

[05:45] Jordan: Quick commercial check — pilot model: typically 4 weeks of testing, reserved capacity option for burst windows, and then if pilot passes we move to a three-month reserved or Dedicated evaluation. Pricing tiers depend on peak committed GPU and token volumes. I'll send pricing options after the call.
[06:03] Elena: Sounds good. For success criteria, let's propose: parity on accuracy (entity extraction F1 within 2% of baseline), 95th latency <250ms for 500-token prompts during 30 qps spike, and structured-output pass rate > 99%. If those pass, we move to a 3-month reserved pilot.
[06:24] Jordan: That seems reasonable, we'll put that in the pilot doc. Any objections?
[06:30] Tom: No objections.

[06:35] Marc: A couple edge questions — what about quantized models? We need to keep costs low; do you run int8 quant models for the assistant?
[06:44] Samir: Redwood supports quantized variants and can route non-critical traffic to Q8/Q4 models. For deterministic function outputs we recommend FP16 or quantized-but-validated models — we'll include a regression check in the harness.
[06:58] Sofia: Data residency — we need backups of logs to remain in EU for some customers. Is that possible?
[07:05] Priya: Yes — Redwood Private and Dedicated both support region pinning and can keep audit logs and backups in EU S3 buckets under your account; we'll document KMS and HSM options.

[07:20] Elena: Timeline, let's align: ArgentCloud can deliver sample anonymized payloads by 2026-05-21, Redwood to deliver harness by 2026-05-24, then we run a benchmark window the week of 2026-05-26, results back by 2026-06-01, decision mid June. Does that work?
[07:40] Jordan: Yes we'll slot those dates. We'll also propose a 90-minute engineering-only kickoff before the benchmark run — to align the harness and sampling.

[07:53] Marc: For the engineering kickoff, who should attend from Redwood? We want someone who knows the runtime internals in case we hit odd latencies.
[07:59] Samir: I'll lead that with one platform engineer, and Jordan will join for baseline config.

[08:10] Elena: Security will want to run a short compliance Q&A after the benchmark — maybe 30 minutes. Sofia will schedule.
[08:18] Sofia: Yep I'll send a Doodle for that.

[08:25] Jordan: I'll recap next steps — send pricing and pilot template (Jordan), benchmark harness + runbook (Samir), ArgentCloud to send sanitized payloads (Marc), we schedule eng kickoff week of 5/26 and security Q&A after benchmark.
[08:40] Tom: One more thing — do you have a pre-built OpenAI-compat shim for our serverless functions? We want minimal changes.
[08:49] Samir: Yes, we have Node/Python shims; we'll drop a small migration snippet that patches existing client calls to point at Redwood endpoints using your existing API keys.

[08:58] Elena: On metrics, will you provide a per-route cost breakdown? We need to know which flows are driving spend.
[09:05] Priya: Redwood Console provides per-route/model token breakdowns and estimated cost per request; we'll show sample dashboards in the pilot.

[09:16] Marc: Regarding function-calling determinism — if the model returns slight variants in ordering or argument types, do you offer a deterministic normalization step?
[09:25] Samir: We have structured-output normalization and canonicalization tools that can reorder fields, coerce types, and flag mismatches. We'll include that as part of the harness validations.

[09:40] Jordan: Okay unless there's anything else, we'll close and confirm deliverables in an email. Thank you everyone.
[09:48] Elena: Thanks, this is helpful. We'll get the payloads over soon.
[09:55] Sofia: I'll follow up with compliance questions.
[10:00] Jordan: Great, end call.

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcriber occasionally swapped acronyms (KV vs KV cache), and some proper nouns may be off.
